note: Every budget was measured on the target PC (S02-S08 one by one, T5 in S10 on 2026-10-13). No limit was changed since the user confirmed them in S01. Numbers are only comparable on the same machine: every run records a machine fingerprint. U3 became 'calibrated' in S11 (2026-10-13); I1 stays 'calibrated-at-limit' (decision pending, see its note). The regression gate (S10, ADR-023: scripts/dev/perf.ps1, tools/perf-compare.mjs) reads 'limit', 'direction', 'status' and 'knownIssues' from this file.

harnessCalibrationS10.note: S10 measured T5 (perf_e2e) and the search matrix (perf_matrix), and built the gate baseline from 3 runs of the whole perf suite on one machine (see docs/steps/S10-perf-harness/perf.md). The 3 runs show how much this machine drifts: run 1 was 1.5-2.5x slower than runs 2-3 on every UI and domain metric (T3 1.86 vs 0.72 ms, U4-PNG 287 vs 121 ms, I3 39 vs 18 ms) while the processor ran at 54-67 percent of its nominal speed; the spread of medians over the 3 runs has a median of 44 percent. That is why the gate compares with a range and reports INCONCLUSIVE when half of the metrics move together. T3, I3, U4-PNG and AB-U1a were over their limits in the slow run only.

uiCalibrationS11.note: S11 optimized U3 with before/after numbers on one build and one day (docs/steps/S11-optimize/perf.md, ADR-024). Before: U3 median 18.9 ms, p95 23.5 ms (5832 components). After the glyph cache in RoiLayerItem: 13.5 / 17.6 ms. After lazy labels and row names in SceneBuilder: 8.75 / 11.2 ms. After the document scene cache: 6.5 / 7.6 ms (this last step targets U3-bg, 17.8 to 7.2 ms; the U3 change is within the drift of the machine). U3 is now calibrated; the test no longer marks it as a known over-budget item. I1 (pan and zoom) also benefits: offscreen p95 8.1 to 4.5 ms in one run; the real-window number of ADR-009 was not re-measured, so I1 keeps its status. No limit was changed.

uiConfirmation.scope: U1a U1b U2 U3 U4 I1 I2 I3 I4 I5 I6
uiConfirmation.note: The user confirmed the UI numbers and the three definitions marked 'definition' below. They stay 'proposed' until S02 and S04 calibrate them.

knownIssuesNote: S10 (ADR-023): metrics that are over budget or slower for a reason we already recorded. The gate (tools/perf-compare.mjs) lists them but does not fail on them. 'source' is the result-file source (ab, matrix, e2e, opencv, halcon, ui-s04, ...), 'idPattern' a regular expression on the metric id. Remove an entry when the issue is fixed; the gate will then enforce the budget again. The B1-B3 entries (ADR-004 section 5, HALCON on the low-contrast, heavy-blur and noise 12 boards) were removed on 2026-10-13 when branch fix/halcon-accuracy fixed them. Budget ids with status 'measured-over-limit' or 'calibrated-at-limit' (now only I1; U3 was fixed in S11) are known the same way without an entry here.

uiCalibration.note: S02 measured U1a, U1b, U4, I1, I2, I5 on one machine (see docs/steps/S02-ui-shell/perf.md for method, machine and caveats). No limit was changed: the user confirmed these numbers in S01. 'measured' holds p95 in ms from the S02 baseline: 'offscreen' is Qt software-raster CPU time; 'window' is the same code in a real window (backing store present included), measured for a subset only. U2, U3, I3, I4, I6 were measured in S04: see uiCalibrationS04.

uiCalibrationS04.note: S04 measured U2, U3, I3, I4, I6 on one machine, offscreen platform only (see docs/steps/S04-presenter/perf.md for method, machine and caveats). No limit was changed. 'measured' holds the range of p95 in ms over 3 runs of the same build. U2, I3, I4, I6 are inside their limits. U3 is OVER its limit at every size that was measured (5832 components: p95 46-61 ms against 16 ms; the cause and the options are in perf.md). The test records U3 as a known over-budget item and does not fail on it. The decision on U3 (cut the cost, or change the definition) is open and belongs to the user. No real-window measurement was made in S04.

searchCalibrationS05.note: S05 measured T3 on one machine (see docs/steps/S05-lattice/perf.md for method, machine and caveats). No limit was changed. 'measured' holds the range over 3 runs of the same build. T3 is inside its limit. The first version of the estimator was over the limit (p95 3.3-3.6 ms over 3 runs); perf.md shows the profile and the changes. The other T budgets need a real back end (S07, S08, S10).

searchCalibrationS08.note: S08 measured T2b with the HALCON back end (3 runs of the same build plus a 4th run of perf_halcon; see docs/steps/S08-halcon/perf.md). No limit was changed. T2b was over its limit in 1 of 3 runs, when the whole machine was slower. HALCON was also measured for T1, T4, T6a, T6b and T7 on the same boards as OpenCV, in the same process (CV-* in the baseline): T1 p95 7.0-22.0 ms, T4 p95 28.6-46.6 ms, T6a 100 percent, T6b p95 0.48 px (limit 0.5), T7 about 3-7 ms per type with one find_shape_models call. These ids keep the S07 OpenCV numbers in 'measured'; whether the two back ends need separate ids is a decision for S10.

searchCalibrationS07.note: S07 measured T1, T2a, T4, T6a and T6b with the OpenCV back end on synthetic boards, 3 runs of the same build (see docs/steps/S07-opencv/perf.md for method, machine and caveats). No limit was changed. 'measured' holds the ranges over 3 runs. All five are inside their limits. The first version of the searcher was over T2a and T4 (p95 263 ms and 120 ms in one run); perf.md shows the change. T7 (library match against N candidate types) was measured too: about 8-9 ms per type, linear in N. Its limit is a proposal in perf.md and is not in this file, because a new limit is the user's decision. T2b needs HALCON (S08); T5 needs the UI path (S10).

budgets.note: Inside the limit since S11 (2026-10-13). S04 measured p95 46-61 ms (median 37-46): the repaint of the whole canvas was 19-30 ms. S11 made three changes (see uiCalibrationS11): the box layer paints small boxes as cached glyphs (one paint 12.5 to 1.15 ms), the scene builder no longer formats a label and a row name for every object, and the document part of the scene is cached. The same machine drifts by about 2 ms between runs; the range is from two runs after the last change.
